text:
Maya: Quick heads-up — after rolling the prefix-cache-aware packing tweak to canary(50%) we saw an unexpected p99 spike on short requests. digested profiler attached but TL;DR: kernel selection churn up when cache-hit-heavy traffic packs with variable prefix lengths. anyone else seeing this?

Josh: I noticed that too. short (<128 tokens) requests have p50 ~18ms same, but p99 jumped from ~28ms -> ~52ms. cache hit ratio went from 40% -> ~72% on canary. looks like batch formation is creating more heterogeneous batches which forces runtime to switch kernels mid-batch.

Anita: likely origin: continuous-batcher now attempts to prefer packing cache-hit prefixes together, but when hits are mixed with misses we end up with sequences with longer effective prefix len distribution. kernel selector picks different GEMM/attention kernel paths per sample which hurts throughput and increases tail latency.

Leo: agree. also the queue policy currently favors fill-rate over latency when prefer_cache_hits=true. that means a request waits for a cache-hit partner to maximize token-util packing; bad for tiny low-latency requests.

Maya: summary of hypotheses: 1) cache-hit-aware packing increases heterogeneity within batches leading to kernel switching overhead; 2) queue policy (wait-for-hit) increases wait time for short requests; 3) token-budget targets (target_batch_tokens) set high -> larger batches with more variety.

Emily: profiler snippet (sample flame) — showing repeated kernel_init calls between token steps:
```
# simplified trace excerpt
batch_start
  kernel_A (0..10)
  kernel_switch -> kernel_B
  kernel_B (11..30)
  kernel_switch -> kernel_A
  kernel_A (31..40)
batch_end
```
This switching cost ~1.6ms per extra switch on our nodes. multiply by 3-5 switches in worst-case batches.

Josh: can we avoid switching by grouping more strictly on effective sequence length or by splitting batches into homogeneous kernel-groups before dispatch? splitting reduces batching efficiency though.

Anita: option list for experiments:
- A: add ``homogeneous_grouping`` step: pre-sort the batch by (cache_hit, effective_prefix_len_bucket) and sub-batch to avoid kernel switching. keep target_batch_tokens constant.
- B: change queue policy to low_wait_for_short (<50ms) for requests with tokens<=64 (fast-path). global target_batch_tokens reduced by 20%.
- C: kernel-guard: detect mixed-kernel batches and automatically mark for immediate dispatch (i.e., avoid runtime switching) — trades off throughput.

Leo: I'd vote for A + B in combo as an initial run. A avoids the kernel churn, B limits waiting for hits. C seems heavy and might be fragile.

Maya: agree. also we should instrument more metrics: per-batch kernel_switch_count, avg_kernel_runtime_by_bucket, wait_time_by_token_bucket, and p99_by_path(serve_with_cache, serve_without_cache). add trace sampling for 1 in 1000 requests to capture full vm/profiler stacks.

Josh: proposed ab-config flags:
```
batcher.pre_sort = true
batcher.pre_sort_keys = ["cache_hit","prefix_len_bucket"]
batcher.max_wait_ms = 50  # for small requests
batcher.target_batch_tokens = current*0.8
```
We'll run on canary (25%) for 12h then 100% for 24h if stable.

Anita: one more note — we should adjust the kernel selector to be less sensitive for tiny sequence lengths (<=32). default path-switch threshold could be bumped so we don't switch for small cost diffs. that should reduce noise.

Emily: I'll add metrics and a flame capture dashboard. can we add a small e2e perf test that simulates high cache-hit ratio with a mix of tiny and medium prompts? current synthetic suite doesn't stress that distribution.

Maya: yes please — Rishi (rishi-bot) can we schedule a job? @rishi-bot schedule perf/sim prefix-hit-heavy 6h now -> produces traces to /perf/canary/1862500000

rishi-bot: scheduled job `perf.sim.prefix_hit_heavy` -> runs for 6h, sampling rate 1/1000, results -> /perf/canary/1862500000. ETA: 6h. :robot_face:

Leo: quick checklist for the experiment:
- deploy pre_sort + small_wait flags to canary(25%)
- enable kernel_switch_count metric
- run perf sim job (Emily/Anita)
- collect p50/p95/p99 for tokens{<=32,33-128,129-512}
- review 24h and decide next step

Josh: I'll own the rollout changes + infra flags. Anita/Emily will own metrics + perf test. Maya to sign off on rollback criteria.

Maya: rollback criteria: p99 for <=128 tokens increases >15% or absolute >60ms OR kernel_switch_count per-batch avg increases >1.5. otherwise hold and iterate.

Emily: noted. I'll post dashboards link once metrics ready. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Leo: small UX note — let's add a short in-console note for customers on canary about "experimental prefix-packing" so support isn't flooded with questions.

Maya: good call. I'll draft a blurb. thanks all.

(reacts: :eyes: from Josh, :rocket: from Emily)
